name: GSA SAM.gov Contracting page on the FPDS transition
title: GSA SAM.gov Contracting page on the FPDS transition
answer: This is a U.S. General Services Administration SAM.gov Contracting page about federal contract award data and the retirement of FPDS.gov search tools. Its most useful point for procurement watchers is that FPDS.gov ezSearch has been retired and all contract awards data searches should now be conducted in SAM.gov, while the FPDS.gov ATOM Feed is due to retire later in FY 2026. Federal users can still manage contract award records with legacy FPDS credentials. The page also notes subcontracting reporting moved from eSRS.gov to SAM.gov.

sections.body: The text is a U.S. General Services Administration SAM.gov Contracting page, harvested on 26 September 2026, although the source URL is fpds.gov. It describes federal contracting search functions, contract award records, subcontract reports, and the transition of FPDS.gov data and eSRS.gov reporting into SAM.gov. It is a system landing and notice page rather than a research report or dataset. It includes operational notices dated June 9, 2026, and later FY 2026.
sections.heading: What this source is

sections.body: SAM.gov is described as a centralized source for finding and bidding on U.S. government contract opportunities, awards and publishing subcontract reports. Users select Contracting from a search box, enter search criteria, and refine by domain such as Contract Awards or Subcontract Reports. The page says the General Services Administration has retired the Electronic Subcontracting Reporting System, eSRS.gov, as part of modernizing federal acquisition systems, and subcontracting reporting is now available in SAM.gov. It also says the FPDS.gov ezSearch feature has been retired, and users should conduct all contract awards data searches in SAM.gov. The FPDS.gov ATOM Feed will be retired later in FY 2026. Federal users can manage contract award records by selecting manage contract awards and logging in with legacy FPDS credentials. The page offers exploration of federal procurement data and contract award records based on awardee, agency, set-asides, and more, with navigation between pre-award and award data where available. It points to detailed information about each Contract Award data element, including format, structure, requirements and FAR references. Federal users can also manage opportunity notices and learn about roles, data standards and notices. The sentence is truncated in the supplied text.
sections.heading: What it says

sections.body: The source gives no numeric figures beyond dates. It states that the FPDS.gov ezSearch feature has been retired, that the FPDS.gov ATOM Feed will be retired later in FY 2026, and that federal users can manage contract award records with legacy FPDS credentials. It states that GSA retired eSRS.gov and that subcontracting reporting is now in SAM.gov. It dates a revision to ISR eligibility logic in the Subcontracting Plan Reporting system to June 9, 2026, and says contractors might see an increased volume of contracts and subcontracts in their Eligible Workspace. It also states that the system is FOR OFFICIAL USE ONLY and subject to monitoring.
sections.heading: Figures and claims worth noting

sections.body: The source does not mention artificial intelligence or the Defense industry. For a reader following AI in Defense, its value is procedural. It shows that federal contract award searches are moving to SAM.gov and that FPDS.gov tools are being retired, so any future tracking of AI-related defense contracts through FPDS data would need to use SAM.gov. It also notes that subcontracting reporting moved to SAM.gov, which matters for following prime and subcontractor activity. It does not provide AI-specific or defense-specific analysis.
sections.heading: What it means for AI in Defense

sections.body: The text is a system landing and notice page, not a dataset or report. It does not mention artificial intelligence, the Department of Defense, DoD contract actions, or vendor performance history at the transaction level. It does not explain how to download or query FPDS data beyond saying searches move to SAM.gov. One notice is truncated mid sentence. The page is operational and transitional, and its most specific dates are June 9, 2026, and later FY 2026. It is published by GSA and is marked FOR OFFICIAL USE ONLY.
